newsitem.title: USA: Gary & Co on Dade Co underwriting team.
newsitem.headline: Gary & Co on Dade Co underwriting team.

text.p: The Dade County Commission on Tuesday approved an underwriting group for a $450 million revenue bond which included Howard Gary & Co, a firm swept up in Miami's corruption scandal, a commission official said.

A lawyer for Gary & Co has said the Miami firm had been an informant for federal investigators. The investigators have said Gary & Co is not a target of its ongoing inquiries into allegations of corruption in City of Miami and Dade County bond deals.

The Miami Herald has reported that federal investigators recorded a conversation in which owner Howard Gary, as well as Calvin Grigbsy, owner of Grigsby & Co, discussed an alleged kickback with a Dade County commissioner.

Gary & Co was removed as senior manager of a Dade County seaport issue earlier this year but was allowed to keep the co-manager's slot on a county solid waste refunding issue for $120 million authorized in recent weeks.

Chip Iglesias, chief of staff for Dade County Commissioner Jimmy Morales, said Morales had questioned the inclusion of Gary & Co in the underwriting group for the $450 million issue before the commission's vote.
The commission also voted to approve a $450 million water and sewer revenue bond, which will be priced in January, Iglesias said.

Iglesias also said the question of whether the role of the two firms in county bond deals was discussed at a meeting of the commission's finance committee but no action had been taken. The committee, which is chaired by Morales, will take up the matter again at its January meeting, Iglesias said. ((-- Michael Connor - Miami newsroom, 305-374-5013))
